entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Courage at its very greatest - the kind that legends are made of.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Sounds heroic - a word at home in battle and legend.
examples: a valiant attempt to prevent the hijack

entries.definition: lacking conviction or boldness or courage
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Gently critical - the courage is missing, but the word feels sorry for the person more than it blames them.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The gentlest way to say *dead* - death softened into rest.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: A gentler way to say *dead* - it softens the statement rather than praising the person.

entries.definition: pass from physical life and lose all bodily attributes and functions necessary to sustain life
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Legal wording: the death is an event on a form.

entries.definition: pass from physical life and lose all bodily attributes and functions necessary to sustain life
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Even shorter and softer than *pass away* - the gentlest way of putting it.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Idleness in a cool, Latin-sounding word - not wanting to make the effort, judged from above.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Like *flatter*, with gentle persuading added - the praise is a lever being pulled.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Formal, as at a ceremony - it lifts praise into the language of religious services.

entries.definition: (used colloquially) having the relationship of friends or pals
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Openly mocking - the rhyming double sound carries the scorn for you.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Sounds a little like therapy talk; it names a kind of person rather than an act.
examples: Saturday's child is loving and giving

entries.definition: marked by refinement in taste and manners
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Praises good taste and manners, but in a stiffly proper way - and it can carry a faint note of pity.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Treats the refusal as rebelling against the people in charge - not just being difficult.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The most scornful of the stubborn words - stubbornness treated as stupidity.

entries.definition: not having enough money to pay for necessities
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: A refined word from books - it holds poverty at a polite distance.
